fileDesc.titleStmt: LETTERS OF TWO QUEENS. ED. BY LT.-COL. THE HON. BENJAMIN BATHURST. LONDON: ROBERT HOLDEN & CO. LTD. 1925.

text.p: Houndslerdyck June ye 10th 1681 .

tic so very long since I have heard from my dear Aurelia that I don't know what to think of it, but now I think ont tic my own faut for I have not yett ansered your to letters I had last the first of which was a very long on & full of news for which I give you a thousand thanks ye to there was but short but you tell me on whom I must lay the faut therefore I say nothing to you. but you will find me very lazy & much to blame not having ritt all this while & I confess I am so but if you knew how little time I have had ever since I came from the hummeling you would not wonder, I have bin heer a week to day last sunday I received yesterday I was at the Hage to see a Princese who
is there three days before she was to se me & ondly just friday & Saturday there has bin company heer every day, but this time I was resolved not to louse another post therefore I ritt this in the morning for that reason. I hope I have said enough to persuade you tic not want of kindness (for that you may always be sure of) but time which has hinderd me all this while assuring you that nothing is nor can ever be capable of changing me who am & shall be ever the same kind constant clorine I always was. For Mrs. Apsley.
Dieren June ye 17 .

You have taken a way of clearing my douts dear husband which would make me your rival if it wear to any but your prince Ziphares but for him you know I have always had a love to great to increase and to natural not to last always & upon to good an account to make you jelouse. but I cant tel wethere the compliments you make your Clorine at the end of your letter are not to great to have so much credit given them but I am good natured enough to believe I have still the greatest shere of your heart & do consent so dear a creature to you & who is so doble dear to me shoud have some part of it, since she has so much of mine. I hope by this time my dear Aurelia is quite well again, & that she does me so much justice to believe my concern was equal to my love which you know is as it ever was & tho you talk at a fine romantic way of your heart I assure you mine will ever be the same & I will hold yours as fast as ever I can for I am resolved if I can keep it I never will part with it while I live & if I die I pretend so much power over it that I would leave it for a legacy to yours and my dear Ziphares.
Pray remember me very kindly to your Mother and Sisters. To Mrs. Apsley.
Edinburgh Sep ye 8.

My dear Sem;dra I do again beg your pardon for being these too or three posts without writing to you but seriously I could not possible help it
but now I must say something in answer to both your letters which I have received since I wrote to you in the first place I must tell you that I forgot to tell you that you should stand for me to Mrs. Doylys child pray remember me to her when you see her & then I must tell you that tho you heard constantly from Pert who had a great many letters to wrote & went often abroad yet she did not go so constantly every day as I did for I rid every day & then I was often with the Duchess & then I took a little time in my closett when I could catch it consider all these things well & forgive your poor Ziphares as to what you desire to know in your other letter I do asure you I do love you dearly & not with that kind of love that I love all others who proffer themselves to be my friends pray therefore dear Sem;dra love me as well as ever be as free with me as ever wrote me all the news you know send me ye Gazett & other printed paypours that are good & forgive & believe your
Ziphares.
pray remember me very kindly to your Mo & tell I will writ to her next post.
Edinburgh Sep ye 16.

My dear Sem dra I have ten thousand millions of pardons to beg of you for mising these too or three last posts & pray forgive me for it was don out of no unkindness to you upon my word, but I asure you I will henceforward wrote every post & I do indeed pity you, for I am very sensible of your great loss my dear Semdra be a little comforted for it may displease God Almighty to see you not submit to his will & who knows but that he may lay some greater afliction on you death is a dept we must all pay when God is pleased to take us out of this wicked world but I hope you will live a great while & yt we shall be happy in seeing one a another tho God & the King only knows when pray remember me kindly to your mother father & brother farewell my dear I love you dearly upon my word & will never change For Mrs. Apsley.
Houndslerdyck June the 13th 1682 .

I am ashamed dear Lady Apsley to have bin so long without ansereing your letter which I received by Sir G. Silvius but the treuth is that since he came into this country last I have never bin long
enough in a place to have time to ritt to any for whilst I was at Bruxells (I spake it to my shame) I never had time to rit neither to the Duke, the Duchess, nor my sister, whom I hope are now with you in England, you may be sure I shoud be very glad your wish could be treu at this time & that I could come to pay my duty to them & at ye same time se the rest of my good friends, but if it cant be presently I hope I shall once find such a time which you may believe will be a very welcome one to me, in the mean time I hope you will believe that as I have bin so I shall endeavour always to show my self to my lives end both to you & all yours for your sake, your very affectionate kind friend
Marie.
Windsor, June ye 12th 1682 .

My dear Semdra. I received yesterday a letter from my Lady Bathurst I do forgive her for not telling me the secret but I asure you I love you
as well as ever I did & I am very sorry you think the contrary I am sure I never intended to do anything that should look like unkindness to you or any of your family & I am extremely sorry if ever I have don anything that you take unkindly I asure you I never did it a purpose & therefore pray forgive me & do me the justice to believe what is a very great truth yt I do love you as well as ever.
Dieren Jully the 25th 1682 .

I have staid all this while in hopes of an ansere to my last letter. but not getting one I sit down now with full intentions to chid you dear Aurelia for I find the changing of your condition has also changed your mind a great deall or else you would have satisfied me before now & all the fine complements in your which letter you rit me since you are married (but before you had mine) will not searve your turn, for you have known this great while or I may better say ever since you knew me that your letters wear always very welcome & never troublesome, & I have told you twenty times that tic impossible for me to rit so often to you as you can do to me for I can never send you news from heance and you can seldom want it where you are so that you have no excuse of your side & I have reason of mine however you
se & have bin I hope a great while very well persuaded that nothing can change me but that whether I wright or no I am & shall be to my lives end ever the same. Now I am in a chiding way I must chid it out once for all but I had almost forgot to say that your not having heard from me was no excuse not to tell me your great afaire as you with reason call it for you knew me enough to trust me if you would have used me like a friend.
St. Jameses Aug ye 14th.

my dear Semdra I have intended ever since I came hither to wrote to you & I hope you will forgive me for not doing it sooner I thank you for your letter & pray ask me what ever questions you will for upon my word I love my dear Semandra as well as ever: since I came to town I am grown a very good Housewife for I am constantly dressed by prayer time & I have bin
very often ready between nine and ten: I wish & yet I know not how to wish you hear because I am sure you had rather be where you are but yet I cant help having a little self interest: all ye news that I know is that Lady Anne Savell was married last thursday to Lt Vaughan: pray remember me very kindly to your Mother & believe me you shall ever find me the same Ziphares I ever was.
since I have wrote my letter I have got a little sister.
Hage December ye 29th 1682 .

your kind letter dear Aurelia puts in a strange impatience to know what it is you dare not writ & I believe it must be of great importance since you ad presently afer that you would put your life into my hands. for god sake put me out of
my pain & let me know it, if ever you have loved me, if ever you have loved your prince, if ever you have loved or do eithere father mothere sister brother, & last of all if you love your dear husband I conjure you to let me know it & yt quikly, or I shall conclude you never did care for me nor for any I have named make no beginning nor ending put no name nor no superscription but put it for me in what you writ to my Mam or let my sister her self send it these, or any other way you can think of so I do but know it. adieu my dear Aurelia by this I shall know if you love me.
pray remember me very kindly to your mothere & believe no body wishes more for the continuance of both your healths then I do. For the Lady Bathurst.
Hague Feb. ye 23rd 1683

I have found to letters of very old date in my standish which makes me believe I have not ansered them for which I ask you a thousand pardons. the first is of the 19th of December I can assure you
dear Aurelia I think all you said very well & am very much of your mind concerning that person you there mention & had I known of the friendship at first I shoud have done all I could in the world to have broke it of but I never knew any thing in the world till such time as she was forbid when I heard it from my sister herself & was very much surprised & troubled to find her concern as great. but then I did not say much because I did not think it nessesery another time you will oblige me very much to let me know if there be any new ones in hand that I may endeavour to stop it if it be not to her advantage or at least do my best for I think nothing more prejudicciell to a young woman then ill company & I hope you will continue your good consells to us both & never flatter neither.

By ye tother of the 2nd of January you tell me to things which must needs be very pleasing to you & then you may be sure thay are so to me: I received to days ago another by which I find you are quick of which I wish you much joy, & hope you will ever have all the contentment imaginable in all things this world can aford & eternal happiness in that which is to come you never need to make excuses to me for aquianting me with your concerns for I take so much part in all that belongs to you that I look upon it as a peace of kindness in you to do so I have been hindered so long in the writing of this that having more to write I have time to say nothing else ondly assure
you of my continueing the same till death - pray remember me as kindly as possible to your Mothere.
Newmarket March ye 21 .

I am very sorry Lady Apsley has bin ill again but I hope now ye spring comes on she will soon recover: this place aford no news but of Races & cock matches which you don't care for. Dr. Lake went last night and will be in town much sooner then this: I am sorry I did not know his wife was ill when he first knew it for I would very
willingly have let him go on such an ocation I shall now be very quickly with you for the Duchess intends to go to moro seven-night I can say no more at this time to my dear Semandra but yt she shall ever find me ye same I ever was. For the Lady Bathurst.
Windsor June ye 4 1683 .

do not acuse your Ziphares without hearing him & indeed you wrong him mightily in saying he is unkind tho what I am going to say may sound like an excuse yet I asure you tic not so: when I was at London ye first time if I had had time I would have made you a visit & ye reason I have not wrote to you all this time was because I was afraid reading might not be good for you & tho you heard not from me yet I enquired of every body how you did & wrote to your mother a purpose therefore do not have so ill opinions of your Ziphares for tho he changes his condition yet nothing shall ever alter him from being ye same to his dear Semandra that he ever was: as to what you say in your last letter about Sr Benjamin I will be sure to speak to the Duke & do all the kindness yt lies in my power but I must needs tell my dear Semandra this that when I first heard this buisnes concerning my self I spoke to ye Duke of my self for Sr Benjamin Bathurst I am very glad you have got so good a friend as my Uncle Rochester for he can do you as much kindness & service as any body & I am sure any thing that I lies in my power shall not be wanting, once more let me beg you not to have any more ill opinions of me but asure yourself yet all ocations I will be ready to show my self your faithful Ziphares: & now I must desire you yt as soon as you have received this you would send
for Mr. Oliver & bid him com hither for tell him I want him mightily to mend one of my gounds & bid him bring me a pair of bodies to wear with a manto.

I believe my dear Semandra thinks me a very strange creature for not having answered your letter in all this while but I do asure you it has not bin my fault for yt day I received it it was so soon after diner yt I could not then possible wrote & after prayers till I went to Whithall I had company with me all day: yeaterday I did intend to have wrote but dining with ye Queen made me so late yt I could have no time before prayers & afterwards again I had company till I went out & therefore pray donot have an ill opinion of me for I do really love you very well & will ever do so & as for ye picture you shall have one very soon & pray believe what I say for it is really true & you shall ever find me your faithful Ziphares.

Why would not my dear Semandra wrote to me before but keep herself uneasy all this while and now I must tell you yt I am not nor never was angry with you in all my life & I asure you no body has ever said anything against you to me & ye reason why I said no more to you yt day you spoke to me was because I can never express my self in words & therefore if ever you have more suspicions of me as I hope you will not after reading this letter let me know them by a letter: but I asure you I love you as well as ever tic true I have sometimes when I do not know it a very grave look which has made others as well as you ask me if I was angry with them yt I looked so gravly on them therefore do not mind my looks for I really look grave & angry when I am not so another thing you tax me of is never sending for you which is a thing I have not don I confess this great but has not bin my fault I asure you for the Prince stays with me every day from diner to prayers & by that time I com from prayers tic half an hour after four & on my playing days from yt time I am always in expectation of company on those days yt I donot play I commonly go to whithall at six so yt yt hour an a half which I have from prayers till I go to the Duchess I
am glad sometimes to get a little of it alone it being the only time I have to myself and for ye other part of it the Prince ether comes to me or I go to him and we stay with one another till I go out thus you see I have told you very freely how I spend my time so you see yt tic not my fault yt I donot send for you because I have hardly a moment yt I can send for you but yt before you can com ether I have grave company or am gon to Whithall but at any time whenever you will com I will see you & shall be very glad of your company & if you cannot com if you will will wrote I shall be very glad of your letters & will answer them very punctualy therefore let me beg you if you love your Ziphares give way to none of these false suspicions of me for I do asure you upon my word I do love you as well as ever & will do so as long as I live: as for ye paypour I signed an sealed I do remember it very well and will be as good as my word in it tho I cannot yet, ye reason I will tell you when I wrote next as for what you desire to know about Sir Benjamin no body has ever said anything against him to me or if it had bin so you may be sure I would first ask him him about it I will now end hoping you are very well satisfied yt I am ye same I ever was & ever will be to ye last moment of my life.
Windsor Jully ye 1.

my dear Semdra not having time last night to wrote to you by your Brother I now send having a purpose a purpose with this that I might not be any longer without telling you yt I do really love you as well as ever I did I will without fail send your letter to my sister to night I am very sorry you could not com yesterday but I hope by Sunday your face will be well again & then that you will com hither to Church dear Semdra I would say more to you but yt tic past ten o'clock & therefore I must go & be dressed but whether my letters be long or short I will ever be the same.
pray remember me very kindly to your mother. For the Lady Bathurst.
Dieren August 25th 1683 .

I write my last in such hast to my dear Aurelia that I had not then time to ansere that I had of
yours & now I have received another since so that I have now to of yours to ansere the first of which was write the day before my sister was to be married, you may believe it was no small joy to me to heer she liked him & I hope she will do so every day more & more for else I am sure she cant love him & without that tic impossible to be hapy which I wish her with all my heart as you may easily imagine knowing how much I love her. by the tothere you tell me of the comitions my sister left with you which I shoud at first have desired you to have done but that she had often bid me employ her & would have it so by all means ye which I did the rathere in hopes of having some comition from her for there is nothing pleases me more then to be so employed, but I don't heer of any yet & indeed this place afords so little of anything but what one has much better in England that I fear I shall not get any at all. adieu dear Aurelia I have this day so many letters to write that I have not time to say any more to you ondly assure you of the continuance of my kindness which nothing but death can ever alter.
Pray remember me very kindly to Lady Apsley.
Hague Nov ye 5th.

I never found it a hard matter to write to my dear Aurelia before, but at present I don't know
what to say for your afliction is so just one can hardly go about to comfort you and indeed upon such ocations tic ondly from God it can come whom I beseech to grant you may bear it like a christian & so as it may sum to your good, as for my own part I assure you I am as sorry for your loss as any body can be which I hope you don't dout, knowing how much I love you. I know tic in afliction friends shoud show them selves & I should be very glad if I knew any way to show you I am so more than you can believe.
Hague April ye 4th 1684 .

I am very sorry to find yt my Lady Apsley has bin so very ill as you say in your letter but I hope it was ondly the cold wethere & yt with the spring she
will recover I am sure if my wishes can contribute to her health she will not want it nor them: as for you dear Aurelia you make me mad with asking pardon for writing a long letter since you may believe thay are very welcome to me I having desired it so often of you for I can compliment with nobody much less with my good friends, I wish I could send you news from heance of any kind, but as you know no body heer so tic impossible: we have ye coldest Easter I think that ever was for it freezes every night still which makes the spring very backward, adieu dear Aurelia believe me ever the same.
Honslerdyck June 9th 1684 .

I have a long while had to of my dear Aurelias leters to ansere which on thing or other has always hindered me doing till this time, on of them is ondly in contradiction of a former letter and the other tells me of your being with child, I wish you better luke then either the Duchess or my dear sister have had you know how dear she is to me and therefore will not dout how much I was troubled for her I am sure if it had bin my self I could not have bin very much more, but I think we have all reason to thank God she is come of as she is which my thinks is almost a miracle to be so well of a dead child. pray remember me very kindly again to my Lady Apsley & believe me as much yours as ever.
The Prince is gone into Brabant so yt I am now alone heer when he comes bake is uncertain for which I am sure you will pity me.
